passages.text: Then Elihu continued: “Hear my words, O wise men; give ear to me, O men of learning.
passages.sermon:
Elihu spoke next.
Elihu addressed the group.
Elihu spoke to wise men.
Elihu said, "Listen to my words."
Elihu spoke to men who have knowledge.
Elihu said, "Pay attention to me."
passages.original: וַיַּ֥עַן אֱלִיה֗וּא וַיֹּאמַֽר׃ שִׁמְע֣וּ חֲכָמִ֣ים מִלָּ֑י וְ֝יֹדְעִ֗ים הַאֲזִ֥ינוּ לִֽי׃

passages.text: For the ear tests words as the mouth tastes food.
passages.sermon:
The ear tests words.
The mouth tastes food.
The ear and the mouth both examine what they receive.
The ear examines words.
The mouth examines food.
passages.original: כִּי־ אֹ֭זֶן מִלִּ֣ין תִּבְחָ֑ן וְ֝חֵ֗ךְ יִטְעַ֥ם לֶאֱכֹֽל׃

passages.text: Let us choose for ourselves what is right; let us learn together what is good.
passages.sermon: Elihu spoke to wise men and men of learning.\r\nHe said, "Let us choose what is right."\r\nLet us learn together what is good."
passages.original: מִשְׁפָּ֥ט נִבְחֲרָה־ לָּ֑נוּ נֵדְעָ֖ה בֵינֵ֣ינוּ מַה־ טּֽוֹב׃

passages.text: For Job has declared, ‘I am righteous, yet God has deprived me of justice.
passages.sermon:
Job is a man who suffers greatly.
Job says, "I am righteous."
Job believes he has done nothing wrong.
Job says, "God has taken away my justice."
Job feels God has not treated him fairly.
passages.original: כִּֽי־ אָ֭מַר אִיּ֣וֹב צָדַ֑קְתִּי וְ֝אֵ֗ל הֵסִ֥יר מִשְׁפָּטִֽי׃

passages.text: Would I lie about my case? My wound is incurable, though I am without transgression.’
passages.sermon:
Job speaks about himself.
Job says he does not lie about his case.
Job says his wound is incurable.
Job says he has no transgression.
passages.original: עַל־ מִשְׁפָּטִ֥י אֲכַזֵּ֑ב אָנ֖וּשׁ חִצִּ֣י בְלִי־ פָֽשַׁע׃

passages.text: What man is like Job, who drinks up derision like water?
passages.sermon:
Job is a man.
Job accepts mockery easily.
Job takes in scorn as if he drinks water.
No other man is like Job in this way.
passages.original: מִי־ גֶ֥בֶר כְּאִיּ֑וֹב יִֽשְׁתֶּה־ לַּ֥עַג כַּמָּֽיִם׃

passages.text: He keeps company with evildoers and walks with wicked men.
passages.sermon: Job keeps company with evildoers.\r\nJob walks with wicked men.
passages.original: וְאָרַ֣ח לְ֭חֶבְרָה עִם־ פֹּ֣עֲלֵי אָ֑וֶן וְ֝לָלֶ֗כֶת עִם־ אַנְשֵׁי־ רֶֽשַׁע׃

passages.text: For he has said, ‘It profits a man nothing that he should delight in God.’
passages.sermon:
Job is a man.
Job said something about God.
Job said, “It does not benefit a man to please God.”
Job claimed, “A man gains nothing by delighting in God.”
passages.original: כִּֽי־ אָ֭מַר לֹ֣א יִסְכָּן־ גָּ֑בֶר בִּ֝רְצֹת֗וֹ עִם־ אֱלֹהִֽים׃

passages.text: Therefore listen to me, O men of understanding. Far be it from God to do wrong, and from the Almighty to act unjustly.
passages.sermon: Men of understanding, listen to me.\r\nGod never does wrong.\r\nThe Almighty never acts unjustly.
passages.original: לָכֵ֤ן׀ אַ֥נֲשֵׁ֥י לֵבָ֗ב שִׁמְע֫וּ לִ֥י חָלִ֖לָה לָאֵ֥ל מֵרֶ֗שַׁע וְשַׁדַּ֥י מֵעָֽוֶל׃

passages.text: For according to a man’s deeds He repays him; according to a man’s ways He brings consequences.
passages.sermon:
God judges every person.
God looks at what each person does.
God gives each person what he deserves.
God repays a man for his actions.
God brings consequences for a man’s ways.
passages.original: כִּ֤י פֹ֣עַל אָ֭דָם יְשַׁלֶּם־ ל֑וֹ וּֽכְאֹ֥רַח אִ֝֗ישׁ יַמְצִאֶֽנּוּ׃

passages.text: Indeed, it is true that God does not act wickedly, and the Almighty does not pervert justice.
passages.sermon:
God is holy and just.
God never does evil.
The Almighty never twists justice.
God always acts righteously.
God never acts wickedly.
The Almighty never perverts what is right.
passages.original: אַף־ אָמְנָ֗ם אֵ֥ל לֹֽא־ יַרְשִׁ֑יעַ וְ֝שַׁדַּ֗י לֹֽא־ יְעַוֵּ֥ת מִשְׁפָּֽט׃

passages.text: Who gave Him charge over the earth? Who appointed Him over the whole world?
passages.sermon:
God rules over all things.
No one gave God authority over the earth.
No one appointed God to rule the whole world.
God holds power by His own right.
God alone governs creation.
passages.original: מִֽי־ פָקַ֣ד עָלָ֣יו אָ֑רְצָה וּמִ֥י שָׂ֝֗ם תֵּבֵ֥ל כֻּלָּֽהּ׃

passages.text: If He were to set His heart to it and withdraw His Spirit and breath, all flesh would perish together and mankind would return to the dust.
passages.sermon:
God is the Creator and Sustainer of all life.
God gives His Spirit and breath to every living being.
If God chooses to take back His Spirit and breath,
then every living creature would die at once.
All people would return to the dust.
passages.original: אִם־ יָשִׂ֣ים אֵלָ֣יו לִבּ֑וֹ רוּח֥וֹ וְ֝נִשְׁמָת֗וֹ אֵלָ֥יו יֶאֱסֹֽף׃ יִגְוַ֣ע כָּל־ בָּשָׂ֣ר יָ֑חַד וְ֝אָדָ֗ם עַל־ עָפָ֥ר יָשֽׁוּב׃

passages.text: If you have understanding, hear this; listen to my words.
passages.sermon: If you have understanding, pay attention now.\r\nListen to my words.
passages.original: וְאִם־ בִּ֥ינָה שִׁמְעָה־ זֹּ֑את הַ֝אֲזִ֗ינָה לְק֣וֹל מִלָּֽי׃

passages.text: Could one who hates justice govern? Will you condemn the just and mighty One, who says to kings, ‘You are worthless!’ and to nobles, ‘You are wicked,’ who is not partial to princes and does not favor rich over poor? For they are all the work of His hands.
passages.sermon:
God is just and mighty.
God does not hate justice.
A person who hates justice cannot govern.
You must not condemn the just and mighty God.
God says to kings, "You are worthless."
God says to nobles, "You are wicked."
God does not show partiality to princes.
God does not favor the rich over the poor.
God made all people by His own hands.
All people are the work of God.
passages.original: הַאַ֬ף שׂוֹנֵ֣א מִשְׁפָּ֣ט יַחֲב֑וֹשׁ וְאִם־ צַדִּ֖יק כַּבִּ֣יר תַּרְשִֽׁיעַ׃ הַאֲמֹ֣ר לְמֶ֣לֶךְ בְּלִיָּ֑עַל רָ֝שָׁ֗ע אֶל־ נְדִיבִֽים׃ אֲשֶׁ֤ר לֹֽא־ נָשָׂ֨א׀ פְּנֵ֥י שָׂרִ֗ים וְלֹ֣א נִכַּר־ שׁ֭וֹעַ לִפְנֵי־ דָ֑ל כִּֽי־ מַעֲשֵׂ֖ה יָדָ֣יו כֻּלָּֽם׃

passages.text: They die in an instant, in the middle of the night. The people convulse and pass away; the mighty are removed without human hand.
passages.sermon:
God rules over all people.
He is just and mighty.
People can die suddenly.
They may die in a single moment.
This can happen in the middle of the night.
Groups of people may tremble and pass away.
The strong and powerful can be taken away.
No human hand causes this.
God alone removes the mighty.
passages.original: רֶ֤גַע׀ יָמֻתוּ֮ וַחֲצ֪וֹת לָ֥יְלָה יְגֹעֲשׁ֣וּ עָ֣ם וְיַעֲבֹ֑רוּ וְיָסִ֥ירוּ אַ֝בִּ֗יר לֹ֣א בְיָֽד׃

passages.text: For His eyes are on the ways of a man, and He sees his every step.
passages.sermon: God watches every person.\r\nGod sees each path a person takes.\r\nGod observes every step a person makes.
passages.original: כִּי־ עֵ֭ינָיו עַל־ דַּרְכֵי־ אִ֑ישׁ וְֽכָל־ צְעָדָ֥יו יִרְאֶֽה׃

passages.text: There is no darkness or deep shadow where the workers of iniquity can hide.
passages.sermon:
God sees everything.
No one can hide from Him.
There is no darkness where evil people can hide.
There is no deep shadow where wrongdoers can escape.
Workers of iniquity cannot find a place to conceal themselves from God.
passages.original: אֵֽין־ חֹ֭שֶׁךְ וְאֵ֣ין צַלְמָ֑וֶת לְהִסָּ֥תֶר שָׁ֝֗ם פֹּ֣עֲלֵי אָֽוֶן׃

passages.text: For God need not examine a man further or have him approach for judgment.
passages.sermon:
God knows every person completely.
God does not need to question anyone further.
God does not require a person to come before Him for judgment.
God already understands each person fully.
passages.original: כִּ֤י לֹ֣א עַל־ אִ֭ישׁ יָשִׂ֣ים ע֑וֹד לַהֲלֹ֥ךְ אֶל־ אֵ֝֗ל בַּמִּשְׁפָּֽט׃

passages.text: He shatters the mighty without inquiry and sets up others in their place.
passages.sermon:
God is all-powerful and just.
God destroys the mighty.
God does not need to investigate them first.
God removes the mighty from their positions.
God appoints other people to take their place.
passages.original: יָרֹ֣עַ כַּבִּירִ֣ים לֹא־ חֵ֑קֶר וַיַּעֲמֵ֖ד אֲחֵרִ֣ים תַּחְתָּֽם׃

passages.text: Therefore, He recognizes their deeds; He overthrows them in the night and they are crushed.
passages.sermon:
God sees what people do.
God knows their actions.
God acts against them at night.
God destroys them.
They are crushed.
passages.original: לָכֵ֗ן יַ֭כִּיר מַעְבָּֽדֵיהֶ֑ם וְהָ֥פַךְ לַ֝֗יְלָה וְיִדַּכָּֽאוּ׃

passages.text: He strikes them for their wickedness in full view, because they turned aside from Him and had no regard for any of His ways.
passages.sermon:
God sees all people.
God punishes the wicked openly.
He does this where everyone can see.
These people turned away from God.
They did not follow His ways.
They did not understand His paths.
passages.original: תַּֽחַת־ רְשָׁעִ֥ים סְפָקָ֗ם בִּמְק֥וֹם רֹאִֽים׃ אֲשֶׁ֣ר עַל־ כֵּ֭ן סָ֣רוּ מֵֽאַחֲרָ֑יו וְכָל־ דְּ֝רָכָ֗יו לֹ֣א הִשְׂכִּֽילוּ׃

passages.text: They caused the cry of the poor to come before Him, and He heard the outcry of the afflicted.
passages.sermon:
God hears the cries of the poor.
God listens to the outcry of the afflicted.
People cause the poor to cry out to God.
God responds to the suffering of the needy.
passages.original: לְהָבִ֣יא עָ֭לָיו צַֽעֲקַת־ דָּ֑ל וְצַעֲקַ֖ת עֲנִיִּ֣ים יִשְׁמָֽע׃

passages.text: But when He remains silent, who can condemn Him? When He hides His face, who can see Him? Yet He watches over both man and nation, that godless men should not rule or lay snares for the people.
passages.sermon:
God is powerful and just.
God can remain silent.
No one can condemn God when He is silent.
God can hide His face.
No one can see God when He hides His face.
God watches over every nation.
God watches over every person.
God does this so that godless people do not rule.
God does this so that godless people do not trap the people.
passages.original: וְה֤וּא יַשְׁקִ֨ט׀ וּמִ֥י יַרְשִׁ֗עַ וְיַסְתֵּ֣ר פָּ֭נִים וּמִ֣י יְשׁוּרֶ֑נּוּ וְעַל־ גּ֖וֹי וְעַל־ אָדָ֣ם יָֽחַד׃ מִ֭מְּלֹךְ אָדָ֥ם חָנֵ֗ף מִמֹּ֥קְשֵׁי עָֽם׃

passages.text: Suppose someone says to God, ‘I have endured my punishment; I will offend no more.
passages.sermon: A person speaks to God.\r\nThe person says, “I have carried my punishment.”\r\nThe person says, “I will not harm again.”
passages.original: כִּֽי־ אֶל־ אֵ֭ל הֶאָמַ֥ר נָשָׂ֗אתִי לֹ֣א אֶחְבֹּֽל׃

passages.text: Teach me what I cannot see; if I have done wrong, I will not do it again.’
passages.sermon:
A person speaks to God.
The person cannot see everything.
The person asks God to teach him what he cannot see.
The person wants to learn from God.
The person says, “If I have done wrong, I will not do it again.”
passages.original: בִּלְעֲדֵ֣י אֶ֭חֱזֶה אַתָּ֣ה הֹרֵ֑נִי אִֽם־ עָ֥וֶל פָּ֝עַ֗לְתִּי לֹ֣א אֹסִֽיף׃

passages.text: Should God repay you on your own terms when you have disavowed His? You must choose, not I; so tell me what you know.
passages.sermon:
God is the judge.
You have rejected His ways.
You want God to repay you on your own terms.
You must make the choice, not me.
Tell me what you know.
passages.original: הַֽמֵעִמְּךָ֬ יְשַׁלְמֶ֨נָּה כִּֽי־ מָאַ֗סְתָּ כִּי־ אַתָּ֣ה תִבְחַ֣ר וְלֹא־ אָ֑נִי וּֽמַה־ יָדַ֥עְתָּ דַבֵּֽר׃

passages.text: Men of understanding will declare to me, and the wise men who hear me will say: ‘Job speaks without knowledge; his words lack insight.’
passages.sermon:
Men who have understanding will speak to me.
Wise men who listen to me will also speak.
They will say that Job does not speak with knowledge.
They will say that Job’s words do not show understanding.
passages.original: אַנְשֵׁ֣י לֵ֭בָב יֹ֣אמְרוּ לִ֑י וְגֶ֥בֶר חָ֝כָ֗ם שֹׁמֵ֥עַֽ לִֽי׃ אִ֭יּוֹב לֹא־ בְדַ֣עַת יְדַבֵּ֑ר וּ֝דְבָרָ֗יו לֹ֣א בְהַשְׂכֵּֽיל׃

passages.text: If only Job were tried to the utmost for answering like a wicked man.
passages.sermon:
Elihu speaks about Job.
Elihu wants Job to be tested completely.
Elihu says Job answers like a wicked man.
Elihu wishes Job would face judgment for this.
passages.original: אָבִ֗י יִבָּחֵ֣ן אִיּ֣וֹב עַד־ נֶ֑צַח עַל־ תְּ֝שֻׁבֹ֗ת בְּאַנְשֵׁי־ אָֽוֶן׃

passages.text: For he adds rebellion to his sin; he claps his hands among us and multiplies his words against God.”
passages.sermon:
Job is a man who suffers greatly.
He speaks many words about his suffering.
He adds rebellion to his sin.
He claps his hands among us.
He multiplies his words against God.
passages.original: כִּ֥י יֹ֘סִ֤יף עַֽל־ חַטָּאת֣וֹ פֶ֭שַׁע בֵּינֵ֣ינוּ יִסְפּ֑וֹק וְיֶ֖רֶב אֲמָרָ֣יו לָאֵֽל׃ס
